title: Expedited Handling Charges on a Bench Work Order
content:
# Desk Standing Rule: Expedited Handling Charges on a Bench Work Order

## The charge

Where a customer of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service asks for a piece to be handled ahead of the queue, the charge for expedited handling is worked out on the ceiling standing on the most recent authorisation the customer has confirmed on the work order, and is priced onto that order as its own line.

The charge for expedited handling is priced only after the work order carries an authorisation the customer has confirmed on the day the expedited handling is taken on.

## The effect on the order

Once the line lands, what the customer owes on the order rises by that amount, and the piece is thereafter handled on the shortened promise the charge pays for. The customer sees the expedited line on their bench bill alongside the priced work.

## Pricing the line

The line is priced by the desk. The desk unlocks the workshop's own tool `charge_expedite_surcharge_af83d9eb` and calls it. One call books a single expedited-handling line against the named work order under the rush charge code, stamped with today's date and accounting period, written as a positive movement.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `service_order_id` | the bench work order record the expedited line is charged to | an id, as returned by the work order lookup |
| `customer_id` | the customer profile the work order belongs to | an id, as returned by the customer profile lookup |
| `surcharge_amount` | the charge for handling the piece ahead of the queue | a positive figure in USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half to even at the cent |

### Return

A one-line confirmation naming the new priced line's reference number, the work order it was charged to and the amount charged in USD to two decimal places. A returned line naming the entry reference is the receipt that the expedited charge now stands on the order.
